item.title: Kimi Antonelli Could Make Formula 1 History This Weekend in Mexico City
item.description: Photo by: MICHAEL JOHNSON Kimi Antonelli is just one race away from potentially making Formula 1 history, and this weekend’s Mexico City Grand Prix could become the defining moment of his young career. The Mercedes superstar enters the 19th round of the 2026 season with an opportunity to secure his first world championship. At just 20 years old, Antonelli is on the verge of becoming the youngest Formula 1 champion ever, potentially rewriting the record books in a season that has exceeded expectations. And after what happened in Austin, the anticipation could not be higher. Antonelli Is Closing In on History Antonelli appeared ready to celebrate his championship at the United States Grand Prix after delivering a commanding victory from pole position. However, Lewis Hamilton’s fourth-place finish and George Russell’s eighth-place result kept the title fight alive for at least another week. Despite missing that first opportunity, Antonelli strengthened his position considerably. The Italian now leads Russell by 123 points and Hamilton by 124 points with five races remaining. He needs only a ninth-place finish or better in Mexico City to guarantee the championship, regardless of where his closest challengers finish. That puts the pressure squarely on his rivals. If Antonelli gets the job done, he will become the youngest world champion in Formula 1 history, surpassing Sebastian Vettel’s record. He would also end Italy’s 73-year wait for a drivers’ championship, with Alberto Ascari last accomplishing the feat in 1953. Can Anybody Stop Mercedes’ Rising Star? Although Antonelli enters the weekend in an incredible position, the job is not finished. Russell and Hamilton still have a mathematical chance to keep the championship alive, but both need a huge result while hoping Antonelli encounters trouble. Meanwhile, Max Verstappen remains a major threat for the race victory. The Red Bull driver has been finding his form recently, making him one of the drivers to watch as the field heads to Mexico. The high altitude at the Autodromo Hermanos Rodriguez also presents a unique challenge, testing engine performance, cooling and aerodynamic efficiency. A Weekend Formula 1 Fans Cannot Miss Antonelli has already won nine races this season, establishing himself as one of the sport’s biggest stars. Now, he has a chance to turn an outstanding campaign into a historic championship. Could Kimi Antonelli officially become Formula 1’s youngest world champion this Sunday? All eyes will be on Mexico City as the Mercedes driver looks to finish the job.

item.title: Ernie Johnson Retiring from ‘Inside the NBA’ as He Reveals Ongoing Heart Issues
item.description: Credit: x; Stephen Lovekin/Getty NEED TO KNOW Ernie Johnson is leaving Inside the NBA The longtime host announced that this season will be his last on the long-running program Johnson, 70, has steered the show for 37 years After 37 years, Ernie Johnson is retiring from Inside the NBA — but he’s not hanging up his bow tie just yet. The longtime host of the TNT-turned-ESPN program — who has deftly led discussions and run interference for analysts Kenny Smith , Charles Barkley and Shaquille O’Neal for decades — announced on Wednesday, Oct. 28 that this season will be his last at the helm. “It’s just time,” Johnson, 70, said in a social media post . “It’s been an honor to share so many nights, decades actually, at the desk with my brothers Kenny, Charles and Shaq. And with our production crews who are so talented and devoted, and I so appreciate the leadership at TNT and ESPN for allowing the show to continue.” He continued, “So why now? Total honesty here. I’ve always prided myself on my preparation. The hours I put in every day getting ready for the next show. I’ve always loved that part of my job. But I always vowed that if that ever became more of a challenge than it is a joy, then I’ll know it’s time to step away.” It’s time. 🤟🤟🏾🤟🏻🤟🏽 pic.twitter.com/h1qNwsnkUY — Ernie Johnson (@TurnerSportsEJ) October 28, 2026 Johnson shared he has been dealing with “heart issues” for nearly two years, having had bypass surgery 14 months ago — but that it’s not the reason why he’s stepping back. “I feel great, so this isn’t a case where my doctor said you need to stop working, nothing like that,” Johnson said. “But here’s the deal. Going through that has made me treasure even more every second with my amazing wife of 44 years, Cheryl Ann, and being Poppy to our five grandchildren.” Shaquille O’Neal, Ernie Johnson, Kenny Smith and Charles Barkley during Game 5 of the 2025 Eastern Conference Finals on May 29, 2025 in New York City. Credit: David L. Nemec/NBAE via Getty Johnson said he wanted to “slow down a bit” to spend more time with his family. The broadcaster added he will “still do March Madness and other projects for TNT and CBS.” Johnson’s announcement may impact at least one other key personality on the show. During an appearance on The Bill Simmons Podcast last month, Barkley teased that the coming year would be Johnson’s final season — and that he planned to follow suit. “Me and Ernie are a package deal,” Barkley told Simmons. Johnson had another way to describe the end of his own era on the program. Follow your favorite athletes on and off the field with PEOPLE’s free sports newsletter — sign up now! “So this is by no means the end, it’s just a turning of the page,” he said. “And I’ll forever cherish every chapter we have written with Inside the NBA .” Read the original article on People

item.description: Manchester United v Brighton & Hove Albion - Carabao Cup Third Round - Getty Images Sport Manchester United's season has gone from bad to worse following the news that star striker Benjamin Sesko is set for a prolonged spell on the sidelines. The Slovenian international, who has been battling a shin issue, is now expected to be out of action until at least January 2027. Major blow for Sesko and Carrick Manchester United have been rocked by the news that Sesko is facing a significant spell on the treatment table, with the forward ruled out until the new year according to talkSPORT . The former RB Leipzig man has endured a frustrating 2026-27 campaign so far, failing to register a single start in the Premier League. His last competitive involvement for the Red Devils came during a disappointing Carabao Cup exit at the hands of Brighton on September 16. With his return now pushed back until at least January, United must navigate a hectic winter schedule without one of their primary attacking weapons. The club's medical team is currently assessing whether this latest setback is related to the shin problem that curtailed his previous season after a heavy collision with Ibrahima Konate during a fixture against Liverpool in May. The injury crisis comes at a precarious time for Carrick, who is under intense scrutiny following a string of poor results. United currently sit 16th in the Premier League table, marking their worst-ever start to a top-flight season. Striker shortage haunts Red Devils Sesko's absence has highlighted a glaring lack of depth in the United attack, particularly after a summer transfer window where they failed to recruit a new centre-forward. The club had hoped to offload Joshua Zirkzee to make room for reinforcements, but the Dutchman remained at the club despite late interest from Everton and Italian side Fiorentina. Last season, United's success was built on a prolific front line where Sesko, Bryan Mbeumo and Matheus Cunha all reached double figures in league goals. Without the Slovenian's presence, the goalscoring burden has shifted heavily onto Mbeumo, who is currently the club's joint-top scorer with four strikes. Financial investment and goal deficit The lack of production from the forward line is particularly concerning given the astronomical sums invested in the squad. item.title: Kyle Larson Could Deliver a Championship Shaking Statement at Martinsville This Weekend
item.description: Photo by: Gary A. Vasquez Kyle Larson is suddenly on the verge of something special, and NASCAR fans could be watching a championship-defining moment unfold this weekend at Martinsville Speedway. After a dramatic victory at Talladega Superspeedway, the Hendrick Motorsports superstar has put himself in an incredible position heading into Sunday’s race. With only two races remaining in the 2026 NASCAR Cup Series Chase, Larson has built a commanding 73-point advantage over his closest championship challengers. Now, the question is whether anybody can stop him. Larson Has the Championship Within Reach Larson’s Talladega victory could not have come at a better time. After watching his championship lead shrink to just five points at Phoenix, the No. 5 team responded with a performance that completely changed the postseason picture. Larson scored valuable stage points, led 23 laps and survived the chaos that makes Talladega one of the most unpredictable tracks on the schedule. His dramatic final-lap move ultimately delivered his first career victory at a drafting track after 59 attempts. That breakthrough could be the momentum Larson needs to finish the job. With a 73-point lead and only Martinsville and Homestead-Miami Speedway remaining, Larson has an opportunity to put even more distance between himself and the competition. Depending on how the points play out Sunday, he could potentially clinch his third Cup Series championship before the season finale. Can Denny Hamlin Keep the Fight Alive? Denny Hamlin remains one of the biggest threats to Larson’s championship hopes. The Joe Gibbs Racing driver has six career victories at Martinsville and knows exactly what it takes to dominate the Virginia short track. However, Hamlin enters the weekend needing a major turnaround. His eighth-place finish at Talladega was respectable, but Larson’s victory widened the gap between them to 73 points. Hamlin needs a strong performance while hoping Larson encounters trouble. Other contenders also face an uphill battle after Talladega’s massive crashes eliminated several championship hopefuls from contention. Martinsville Could Change Everything Martinsville presents a different challenge from Talladega, putting a premium on braking, tire management and track position. Larson has already proven he can win under pressure. Now, he has an opportunity to deliver another statement when the championship stakes are enormous. If Larson dominates again, the championship battle could effectively be over before Homestead. NASCAR fans should be watching closely: Larson could be just one race away from putting the rest of the field out of reach.

item.title: NASCAR Black Flag Controversy Sparks Debate After Talladega
item.description: Photo by: Gary A. Vasquez NASCAR found itself at the center of another controversy following Sunday’s YellaWood 500 at Talladega Superspeedway, as officials revealed just how close they came to handing out black flags to a large portion of the field. The controversy came from an aggressive fuel-saving strategy that caused drivers to slow down significantly during the opening stage. While saving fuel can provide a major advantage at superspeedways, the pace became slow enough that NASCAR officials felt they needed to intervene. NASCAR Warned Teams About Potential Black Flags NASCAR vice president of racing communications Mike Forde explained on the organization’s Hauler Talk podcast that approximately 75% of the field had fallen below the required minimum speed at one point during Stage 1. Officials sent a message to teams warning them to increase their pace or face potential penalties. The warning worked, and drivers picked up the speed before NASCAR issued any black flags. The situation raised questions about how far teams should be allowed to push fuel-saving strategies before they begin affecting the quality of the racing. Fuel mileage has become an important part of superspeedway competition, where drivers often try to stretch their fuel loads to gain an advantage during pit stops. However, Sunday’s situation showed that NASCAR has limits when it comes to how slowly cars can circulate around the track. Kyle Larson’s Finish Adds to the Controversy The black-flag discussion was not the only officiating debate to emerge from Talladega. Kyle Larson’s dramatic victory also sparked controversy over whether his car went below the double yellow line during his final-lap charge. NASCAR reviewed the incident and determined that Larson’s tires had not crossed completely below the line. Officials explained that a portion of the tire remaining on the line meant the move did not warrant a penalty. The decision preserved Larson’s victory over teammate William Byron, but it also drew criticism from drivers and observers who questioned the consistency of the rule’s enforcement. NASCAR Faces Questions Moving Forward With fuel-saving tactics and the yellow-line rule both generating discussion, NASCAR has plenty to consider as the season approaches its conclusion. The black-flag warning demonstrated that officials were prepared to intervene when the racing pace became unacceptable. However, the weekend also highlighted the importance of clear and consistent rule enforcement. As the championship battle continues, teams will be watching closely to see how NASCAR handles similar situations in the races ahead.

item.title: Brazil reach World Cup and FIFA U-15 Festival quarters on penalties
item.description: Brazil reach World Cup and FIFA U-15 Festival quarters on penalties Guilherme Dalla Déa, head coach of the U-15 national team Credits: Staff Images / CBF Brazil knocked out Venezuela on penalties on Wednesday afternoon (28) to advance to the quarterfinals of the FIFA U-15 World Cup and Festival. In Baku, Azerbaijan, the Seleção played out a goalless draw before winning the penalty shootout 10–9. Goalkeeper Arthur Lourenço made a crucial save from Venezuela's ninth penalty, while Gabriel Keven converted his spot kick to secure a place in the next round. Brazil will face the Czech Republic early on Thursday (29), at 4:30 a.m. Brasília time, for a place in the semifinals. In the competition, the Czechs have recorded the following results: 5–0 wins over Sri Lanka and Togo, a 9–1 win over Cuba, a 14–1 win over the U.S. Virgin Islands, 5–1 wins over Jamaica and Angola, and a 5–3 win over Italy. THE COMPETITION The FIFA U-15 World Cup and Festival uses a different format from traditional football: teams play eight-a-side matches consisting of two 20-minute halves, with unlimited substitutions. The competition brings together national teams from different continents and was created to provide more opportunities for international experience and player development in this age group. In the first stage, teams play four or five group matches. The results determine how participants are divided into six performance tiers for the next stage. All national teams will continue playing until the event concludes on October 30, with champions crowned in each tier. The winner of Tier A will be recognized as the FIFA U-15 World Cup and Festival champion. This article was translated into English by Artificial Intelligence. Exhausting 3-2 win in last 16 at SW Bregenz Our boys made life difficult for themselves in the UNIQA ÖFB Cup on the shores of Lake Constance by being wasteful with a host of scoring opportunities. Nevertheless, they managed to win 3-2 against a spirited Bregenz side to enter the draw for the quarter-finals on Sunday. Match summary 2' – Fast start Less than two minutes in, our attacking players showed exactly what they had in mind. Edmund Baidoo played a through ball to Karim Konate, who danced past goalkeeper Aizawa before slotting the ball inside the far corner (2'). 12' & 23' – further chances Danny Röhl’s side maintained their momentum. Konate came agonisingly close to a second goal, while a header from left-winger Yorbe Vertessen - set up brilliantly by Stevie Lainer - was denied only by the goalpost. 33' – pegged back An old football adage proved to be true as Omotehara appeared up front, connected with a cross from the right, and scored a surprise equaliser (33').We restored the lead before the break though as Vertessen latched onto a quickly taken free-kick from Krätzig - catching the Bregenz defence in a state of disorder - and fired a shot from 16 yards out inside the near post. Restart & 57' – Lazio slayer shocks Bregenz There was no real change in the second period. Our side created high-quality chances almost by the minute. The best of these fell to Baidoo - who narrowly missed the target following a slip-up by Aizawa - and Lainer, who arrived just a fraction too late at the far post to tap the ball in. item.description: Bayern Munich boss Vincent Kompany is currently recovering in hospital after collapsing during a training session -Credit:Stuart Franklin - UEFA, UEFA via Getty Images Vincent Kompany is believed to have dislocated his shoulder when he collapsed during a Bayern Munich training session five days ago. Kompany remains hospitalized in Munich as doctors work to determine what triggered his collapse, which resulted in the former Manchester City captain being swiftly airlifted to the hospital. Physicians treating the Belgian have reportedly been examining a potential neurological issue during his period of illness - keeping him away from the sidelines since he oversaw Bayern's UEFA Champions League draw with Arsenal last week. Thierry Henry addresses Ballon d'Or criticism after Lamine Yamal and Kate Scott remarks Fleetwood Town boss opens up on Mikel Arteta's reaction after Arsenal cup exit -Credit:F. Noever, FC Bayern via Getty Images Bild reports that Kompany has also experienced seizures following his fall, while also claiming the condition is not considered life-threatening, with both a heart attack and stroke having been ruled out. The 40-year-old is not anticipated to return to the dugout for several weeks as his recovery continues. Interim manager Aaron Danks offered an update on Tuesday via The Mirror : "It looks like he's getting better every day. That's positive. But there is no major news regarding his diagnosis or his return to work." Harry Kane, who claimed the Ballon d'Or with Kompany at the helm at the Allianz Arena, revealed he had been in touch with the Belgian ahead of his historic night. The Englishman said: "He actually phoned me, phoned me bright and early at 9am (Monday). I was just out of bed thankfully, so I was able to answer it. item.description: After a penalty thriller, Brazil reach U17 Women's World Cup quarter-finals In an evenly matched contest that saw the lead change hands, Brazil come from behind and Poland equalize in regulation time, the Amarelinha secured their place in the quarterfinals of the FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup. Led by coach Rilany Silva, Brazil came through the round of 16 in Morocco on Wednesday (28), winning in sudden-death penalties, with goalkeeper Nathy’s final save proving decisive. The match began with possession evenly shared between the two teams. In the 11th minute, Greise Kelly received the ball on the right, cut inside and shot left-footed. The ball deflected off the goalkeeper’s foot, hit the post and went in. Poland combined well inside the Brazilian penalty area, producing dangerous shots. Nathy made some good saves, but the Polish pressure paid off in the 33rd minute when Nicola Galuszka evaded her marker on the edge of the box and fired over the goalkeeper after a deflection off Kaillany Ranifah. Keeping up the momentum, Poland took the lead less than two minutes later, with Zofia Burzan firing across goal, also from the right. The first half, which featured two incidents reviewed by the officials, ended with an intense 10 minutes of stoppage time. Marcela Bontorim and Greise Kelly led Brazil’s attack, linking up with Helena, Carol Melo and Sofia, but the best chance fell to Pepê, who picked up a loose ball inside the box but sent her shot over the bar. Comeback and equalizer After the break, with Poland ahead, the Amarelinha maintained the attacking intent they had shown in stoppage time. On a quick counterattack, Greise delivered a low cross to Marcela Bontorim, who got ahead of the defender and gave the goalkeeper no chance. Brazil’s women’s team defeated Poland in the round of 16 of the U-17 World Cup in Morocco Credit: Fabio Souza/CBF With the scores level, Brazil stayed focused on qualification and took the lead in the 70th minute. The move began with a high cross from the right. Greise headed it, the goalkeeper parried, and Pepê pounced on the rebound to score the Amarelinha’s third. Ten minutes after Brazil took the lead, Poland equalized. A through ball down the middle sent Burzan clear of the Brazilian defense and, one-on-one with goalkeeper Nathy, she slotted the ball into the left corner for her second goal of the match and Poland’s third. In the penalty shootout, Indy, Pepê, Greise and Marcela Bontorim all converted. Brazil had the advantage after goalkeeper Nathy saved Poland’s first penalty, but Helena missed Brazil’s final kick. In sudden death, Gigi Pires, Isa Rech, Yasmin Queiroz and Sofia Gamonal scored for Brazil, and Nathy made her fourth save against Poland, sealing the Brazilian victory. Having qualified for the quarterfinals of the FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup, the Amarelinha will face either China or France, who play tomorrow at noon. item.description: Bayern Women fight back to deny Real Madrid in Champions League thriller Bayern Munich had to work their way out of trouble before they could make a game of it. Two goals down inside 22 minutes, they looked vulnerable against a Real Madrid side that punished their slow start. But Edna Imade and Momoko Tanikawa brought Bayern back, and the hosts finished a breathless night wondering how they had not found a winner. The 2–2 draw at Sportpark Unterhaching kept Bayern unbeaten in their first three UEFA Women’s Champions League league-phase matches. It also extended their unbeaten home record in the competition’s group and league phases to 17 games. Yet, given how much control they eventually established, this felt like a point gained and two dropped. Bayern finished with 64 per cent possession, 16 attempts on goal and seven corners. Real managed seven shots and none from the corner spot. The numbers reflected the shift in the game: Real made their early chances count, but Bayern spent much of the second half pushing for a winner. Real strike first… and then again Real needed just seven minutes to take the lead. Linda Caicedo reached the byline and cut the ball back into the area, where captain Athenea del Castillo finished to put the visitors ahead. Bayern had plenty of time to respond, but their early possession did not translate into enough clear chances. Klara Bühl and Franziska Kett looked to create openings from the left, only for their deliveries to go without a Bayern player in the middle. Real were more clinical. In the 22nd minute, former Bayern midfielder Arianna Caruso delivered a free-kick into the box. María Méndez sent the ball back across goal, and Lineth Beerensteyn rose to head home. The former Bayern forward doubled Real’s lead against her old club, leaving the hosts with a steep climb before half-time. Bayern needed a response, and Imade supplied it. In the 31st minute, Bühl’s corner found the forward, who rose above the defence to power a header into the net. The goal gave Bayern a foothold in the match, and their attacking play grew more purposeful. Pernille Harder sent a chance over the bar from Linda Dallmann’s delivery, while Bühl and Dallmann also threatened before the break. Bayern had created opportunities, but they went into half-time still chasing the game. Tanikawa changes the mood Bayern did not wait long to level the score after the restart. Seven minutes into the second half, Dallmann tested goalkeeper Merle Frohms, who saved the initial effort. Tanikawa collected the rebound, made space for herself and curled a left-footed shot into the top corner. At 2–2, the game had taken on a different feel. Bayern were no longer chasing a two-goal deficit; they were looking for the goal that would complete the turnaround. item.title: Josh Heupel updates status of DeSean Bishop
item.description: Oct 24, 2026; Columbia, South Carolina, USA; Tennessee Volunteers running back DeSean Bishop (18) is tackled by South Carolina Gamecocks defensive back David Bucey (9) during the second half at Williams-Brice Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Jim Dedmon-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect It would appear that DeSean Bishop has dodged a bullet on the injury front. The star Tennessee running back exited the South Carolina game late in a key spot with what appeared to be an ankle issue. Bishop was unable to return, missing out on a key fourth down that could have put the game on ice. “We feel like he’ll be in a good spot for next week,” Josh Heupel said on Wednesday. “He got some work today, we limited him some today. Part of that was the ankle, but part of that’s just the volume that he’s gotten in the early part of the conference play, too.” Bishop has handled 32 carries in each of the last two weeks, running for 279 yards and three touchdowns. He’s up to 171 carries on the year, running for 957 yards and 11 scores. The former walk-on is closing in on some career school rushing records with four regular season games remaining in his junior season. However, just as we saw in 2024 with Dylan Sampson, load management is a real thing this time of year. Tennessee ended up running Sampson into the ground during that season, and a late-season injury sidelined him in the College Football Playoff matchup at Ohio State. “DeSean is a massive part of our football team and has played at a really high level,” Heupel said. “He’s got a chance to heal up this week, too, and we’re gonna need him at his best as we go down the stretch.” Tennessee has been able to get Javin Gordon back in the mix over the last couple of weeks, while Daune Morris continues to be a solid option as well. For Tennessee to be at their best though, they need No. 18 wearing down defenses late. Bishop has a full bye week before returning to action next weekend against Kentucky.

item.title: Mike Rhoades wants a 'tough' identity for Penn State basketball
item.description: STATE COLLEGE — If nothing else, Mike Rhoades wants this year's edition of Penn State basketball to be tougher. The fourth-year head coach spoke at local media day on Wednesday, Oct. 28, inside the Bryce Jordan Center, where an almost entirely new roster is set to take the floor Nov. 2 against Canisius for its season opener. During his presser, Rhoades was asked what he wants the identity of this year's team to be "Tough. We got to be tough and physical," Rhoades said. "We may be different and look differently than some other teams in our league, but when it comes down to it, we got to be tough. and I don't mean dirty in a bad way, but dirty and grimy and and fight every possession, fight like crazy every possession." After opting for a freshman-heavy roster last season, Rhoades, general manager Scott Pera and the staff changed the approach, building through the portal to get players with more experience and, hopefully, more fortitude. The result is a 2026-27 roster with five players listed as a senior or older, and three true freshmen. "We made a point to get mentally, physically tougher guys," Pera said. "Usually old age and character provide that, they come hand in hand. That's what we tried to do, and I think they're a really good group of kids." More PSU Hoops: After starting at zero, Tanisha Wright built Penn State women's basketball from scratch Penn State does have some toughness among the returners with Josh Reed, who's eligible following the court ruling for the recruiting class of 2022, and Ivan Jurić, who'll be a second-year starter after a year of banging in the Big Ten as a true freshman. Throw in the the college experience of grad students Thomas Allard and Dasante Bowen, along with Chambersburg native Brant Byers coming from NCAA Tournament darling Miami (Ohio), and the Nittany Lions have a more battle-tested and experienced roster on the floor this year. Will that transition to the season, especially during Big Ten play? The game results will provide that answer. item.title: Bayern coach Kompany leaves hospital after meningeal irritation
item.description: FILE PHOTO - Bayern Munich coach Vincent Kompany is pictured ahead of the German Bundesliga soccer match between FC Augsburg and Bayern Munich at WWK-Arena. (is associated with: «Bayern coach Kompany leaves hospital after meningeal irritation») Tom Weller/dpa Bayern Munich coach Vincent Kompany has been released from hospital five days after collapsing during a training session. Head of Sport Max Eberl told broadcaster ARD on Wednesday that Kompany had been suffering from meningeal irritation, which if untreated can become meningitis. The meninges are the membranes around the brain and spinal cord. Holders Bayern were hosting second division Magdeburg in the German Cup second round on Wednesday, with Kompany missing his second straight game. Assistant Aaron Danks led the team again having masterminded a 3-1 win at Freiburg at the weekend. An emergency doctor was called to training after Kompany's collapse. He had been feeling ill for several days. "They found out what it is. It is a meningeal irritation that brought on the incident last Friday," Eberl said. "Honestly, he is doing as well as can be expected. He has been discharged from hospital today, which is the biggest and best news for all of us." Eberl said that the Belgian would now complete his rehabilitation at home and needed plenty of rest. Danks will stay in charge until further notice, which could include Saturday's Bundesliga table-topping clash at home to Borussia Dortmund. Danks had visited Kompany before his discharge from hospital. Eberl rejected the theory that the coach's collapse was also a consequence of excessive pressure. "It is an illness. Anyone of us can get it. It has nothing to do with the pressure we face in the Bundesliga," the 53-year-old said. Eberl spoke of "a difficult time" for Bayern. "You notice how the club is coming together," he said. The German double winners are also currently without influential midfielder Joshua Kimmich following the death of his father.

item.title: World Wide Wob explains walking away at the height of his account’s popularity
item.description: Last summer, after the New York Knicks won their first NBA title in 53 years, NBA X/Twitter personality and lifelong Knicks fan World Wide Wob ended his watch, leaving behind an X account with over 1 million followers. Wob, whose real name is Rob Perez, got his start in the NBA space selling tickets, before later returning to his true passion, covering the NBA. His career includes stops at Barstool Sports, The Big Lead , Fox Sports, the Action Network, SportsGrid, FanDuel, Underdog, and Bleacher Report. The 2026-27 NBA season began last week, and with people on social media wondering where World Wide Wob was, Perez recently talked to Front Office Sports about walking away from his popular account. “Nothing special, just a combination of events,” Perez said of what led to his decision to stop posting on the account. “The Knicks finally winning the title/freeing me from these lifelong shackles, X pivoting its primary content model to a For You recommendation algorithm, the turnover inside X’s sports department and not knowing anyone who works there anymore after the acquisition, and uncompetitive creator earnings compared to other platforms all led to general apathy towards continuing to produce the high-quality content I once did. I spent all day, every day, pouring resources into its creation for about 15 years straight, so this felt like the right time to embrace the burnout.” My watch has ended. Thanks for everything. — Rob Perez (@WorldWideWob) June 14, 2026 Perez didn’t rule out a return to X in the future if a future version of the app/website was one that inspired him to create. He credited having enough financial stability to walk away at 39 years old to “good timing” and creating his own luck, before saying that he’s still covering L.A. police chases on Twitch, running the merch site associated with his Twitch account, and posting some NBA-related content on Threads. The content creator also touched on two of the NBA’s biggest developments since he’s been away: Mark Walter’s fire sale of the Los Angeles Lakers and NBA commissioner Adam Silver’s heavy-handed punishment for Steve Ballmer and the Los Angeles Clippers for salary cap circumvention. “Jeanie Buss is one of the most important people to enter my life, so I hope whatever resolution comes from all the lawsuits keeps her connected to the Lakers franchise, which I know she loves so, so much,” Perez said. “As for the Clippers, they simply got sloppy. There’s always been a ton of gray area re: cap circumvention, but when you leave a blood trail the way that they did—they can’t be surprised if/when the axe falls. item.description: Leeds United Face £2.6m Midfield Battle: Is Farke Right To Push Ahead? Leeds United have collected 11 points from eight Premier League matches this season, winning twice, drawing five times and losing once. Daniel Farke’s side have scored nine goals and conceded six, but five draws highlight the need to turn disciplined performances into more victories, particularly when matches demand greater control in midfield. Their midfield already offers several options. Captain Ethan Ampadu provides defensive cover, Ilia Gruev brings energy, while Anton Stach adds physical presence. Ao Tanaka and Sean Longstaff give Farke further alternatives, although the demands of a Premier League campaign leave little room for complacency over squad depth. With Leeds balancing domestic fixtures and player fitness, another defensive midfielder could give Farke greater flexibility. A player who can recover possession, cover ground and protect the back four would help the existing options manage the workload without forcing the manager to compromise his preferred combinations. Leeds United face competition for a January midfield target According to Sport Witness , citing reporting from Africa Foot, Leeds have opened discussions over Maccabi Tel Aviv midfielder Issouf Sissokho. The report says the Whites initiated contact on October 20 and are preparing an offer for January, but Levante and Sporting Braga have entered the race. Levante have reportedly contacted the 24-year-old Malian’s agent and are preparing a bid worth around £2.6 million. Transfermarkt values Sissokho at approximately £1.5 million. His contract runs until 2027, with an option for another year, and he joined Maccabi as a free agent in 2024 after playing for Bordeaux. He has since made 97 appearances for the Israeli club. item.description: Source: headlinephotos/Depositphotos Bryson DeChambeau has become one of the most important figures in LIV Golf’s fight to survive beyond 2026. The two-time U.S. Open champion has continued expressing support for the breakaway league, even as financial uncertainty and high-profile departures threaten its proposed relaunch. His next career decision could influence whether LIV Golf retains the star power needed to attract fans and commercial backing. DeChambeau has also secured a return to the DP World Tour, adding another dimension to his plans. With LIV’s future approaching a critical deadline, his actions are attracting renewed attention across professional golf. Yet his long-term playing commitments remain unconfirmed. DeChambeau continues supporting LIV Golf despite mounting uncertainty DeChambeau has repeatedly argued that LIV Golf deserves an opportunity to establish a sustainable business model. In August, he asked the golf world to remain open-minded about the league and give it another chance after Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund decided to end its financial support beyond the 2026 season. That position has gained significance as LIV attempts to secure a future under a proposed restructuring plan. The league filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection in September and has pursued new investment intended to support a revised competition model. Recent reporting indicates that DeChambeau remains involved in efforts to make the proposed LIV 2.0 relaunch work. ESPN, as reported by other outlets, has described him as committed to LIV and working behind the scenes, although he has not publicly confirmed a final decision on his participation in 2027. His continued support does not automatically guarantee that he will sign a new agreement. DeChambeau’s contractual position, the league’s revised financial terms and the future competitive opportunities available to him all remain important factors in determining his next move. His DP World Tour commitment adds another dimension DeChambeau has confirmed that he will compete in the Nedbank Golf Challenge in South Africa from December 3–6, 2026. The event, played at Gary Player Country Club in Sun City, will be his first non-major DP World Tour start since 2022. The commitment is significant because it gives the American a confirmed competitive appearance beyond LIV’s 2026 schedule. Reports have also indicated that his representatives explored the possibility of additional DP World Tour starts, although those discussions do not establish that he intends to leave LIV. The DP World Tour’s position has complicated the picture. Chief executive Guy Kinnings has said players who choose LIV Golf in 2027 will not be able to compete on the DP World Tour, requiring players to choose between the two circuits. DeChambeau’s December appearance confirms one event on his schedule but does not establish where he will play throughout 2027 or whether he will accept LIV’s proposed terms.
